system.description:
• You protect the dead from those who would misuse them, and oppose unlawful undead wherever they appear. The morally lightest path: you use death magic to ensure the dead rest as they should.
  • Warden's Strike
  • A creature you damage with a Necromancy spell makes a Will save against your spell DC or can't use its drains or its auras (any ability named an Aura, Frightful Presence and Stench) until the end of its next turn.
  • A creature of higher Level than you saves with Advantage; a solo shakes this off (see Solo Creatures, Book IV).
  • Undead you destroy can't rise again.
  • Undead you did not create make their saves against your Necromancy spells with Disadvantage (never against an effect that kills outright)
  • When you destroy an undead creature, all undead you control within 30ft regain 1d6 HP
  • From 9th level, each enemy within 10ft of that creature makes the same save
  • Deathwatch
  • Advantage on checks to identify, research, or communicate with undead
  • You always know whether a corpse has been subjected to necromantic magic and approximately when it was raised
